label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — resolved sink value is rememberMeKey = Integer.toString(randNumber) where randNumber = new java.util.Random().nextInt(99). The insecure RNG java.util.Random generates the rememberMeKey which is used as a remember-me cookie value (line 97-98: new Cookie(cookieName, rememberMeKey)) and stored in session (line 101). Weak RNG feeding remember-me tokens is explicitly flagged as TP per policy. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value at lines 106-111 is the concatenation including rememberMe.getValue() which equals rememberMeKey. Although rememberMeKey is derived from Random, the cookie value param (from which rememberMeKey is constructed via the cookie lookup loop) originates from request.getCookies()[i].getValue() (line 57), which is attacker-controlled since clients can craft arbitrary cookie values. The tainted value reaches response.getWriter().println() without HTML encoding, enabling reflected XSS. Case TP: at least one alert-TP (both are alert-TP).
